extra.message: The unauthenticated /signup endpoint takes form.registration_code.data and interpolates it directly into a raw SQL string via an f-string passed to session.execute(text(...)). An attacker can inject SQL (e.g. ' OR '1'='1) to bypass registration-code validation and extract data from the database.

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: The /search endpoint reads request.args.get('search') and concatenates it into a raw SQL fragment using text(f"text like '%{search_param}%'"). User-controlled input is executed as SQL, allowing SQL injection.

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: The 404 error handler builds a template from user-controlled data: render_template_string(f"{error}. Requested URL was {request.path}"). request.path is attacker-controlled, so requesting a path such as /{{7*7}} causes Jinja2 to evaluate the expression, yielding server-side template injection and remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: before_request deserializes the attacker-controlled 'preferences' cookie using pickle.loads(b64decode(...)). Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution; a crafted cookie can run commands as the server user.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: download() calls urlopen(url) on a URL taken from the /account/image form (ImageForm.url, only format-validated). An authenticated attacker can supply internal URLs (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:80/, http://169.254.169.254/) to perform server-side request forgery, and the fetched response is stored and returned to the client.

extra.message: Note text is rendered with the Jinja 'safe' filter ({{ note.text | safe }}), disabling HTML escaping. extra.message: render_table(personal_notes, safe_columns=['text']) marks the user-controlled note 'text' column as safe, disabling autoescaping and allowing stored XSS when notes are displayed.

extra.message: POST /account copies every non-None field from AccountForm directly into current_user.__dict__ (current_user.__dict__.update(filtered_values)), including the 'is_admin' BooleanField, and then persists it. A normal user can POST is_admin=true to grant themselves admin privileges (mass assignment privilege escalation). The route also lacks @login_required.

extra.message: No CSRF protection is configured anywhere: the app never initializes Flask-WTF CSRFProtect, all forms derive from wtforms.Form (not FlaskForm), and templates contain no csrf_token. State-changing endpoints such as POST /notes, /account, /account/image, /notes/<id>/delete, /darkmode and /registration-codes can be triggered cross-site with the victim's session cookie.

extra.message: Flask's session-signing secret key is hardcoded (app.secret_key = "super secret key"). Anyone with source access can forge signed session cookies / flask-login 'remember' tokens and impersonate users, including the admin.
